pr_body:
Fixes #96150.

Prior to this patch, it was possible for a server for tenant 123 to perform RPCs to a server for enant 456.
This patch disables that.

Release note: None
Epic: CRDB-23559

issue_context.title: rpc: we're not enforcing one tenant not talking gRPC to another tenant
issue_context.body:
A tenant is supposed to only be able to make RPCs to servers from the same tenant, and to KV. But we're missing checks for the first part - as far as CRDB is concerned, I think one tenant can call into any other. In CC we have network-level protection against this.

I've briefly looked into adding the missing checks, but I failed to do something good with the current code structure. There's [this code](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/9fc497abc81e851d441733a019c515464c6ff742/pkg/rpc/auth.go#L142-L150) which deals with authenticating the caller, but as written it doesn't even return a tenant ID when the receiver is a tenant server, so the [authorization code](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/9fc497abc81e851d441733a019c515464c6ff742/pkg/rpc/auth.go#L68) is inhibited.

cc @ajstorm 


Jira issue: CRDB-23525

review_comments: what advantage does bypassing authorization checks here give us?

Successfully authenticated node-node sessions and root/node client principals have access to all the RPCs.  This has been true through the history of CockroachDB.  

We could change this by introducing a more granular authorization model for RPCs, but that sounds like a new feature/project which would deserve some thinking.
